title: Canonical source and coefficient transports for smooth purity
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, schemes $X,Y$ on which $\ell$ is invertible, and $f:X\to Y$. Use the intrinsic integral, rational and common-stage categories [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], the actual completed tensor and pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and the existing signed root lines [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. For $d\geq0$ define $H_E(K)=E_X(d)[2d]\otimes_E^L Lf^*K$, with the shift on the coefficient line. Its finite coefficient-extension comparison is the actual tensor comparison, coherent scalar shift, scalar root-line comparison and pullback comparison, in that order. The general scalar shift is pinned by localizing the integral ordinary-to-completed shift at degree one; other integers use shift coherence. Define the common-stage source with the shifted line at the least finite stage and tensor it with the literal-stage pullback; its comparison with the source over the input object's own stage retains the coefficient associators, the line comparison, and the identity-transition unitor. On the integral finite-Tor domain [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], the completed-to-ordinary tensor comparison is the localization of the canonical strict quotient augmentation on good K-flat representatives: its product component is the tensor of the quotient maps, and its second Roos cone component is zero. These comparisons use the ordinary coefficient operations of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] and are fixed by these representative formulas.

proof.text: Construct the strict augmentation as the quotient completion unit whiskered by the ordinary total tensor, followed by the Roos image of the normalized tensor tower isomorphism. Its product coordinates are the tensor of the quotient units and its shifted coordinate is zero, by lem-pur-strict-tensor-augmentation-coordinates. This construction works on all complexes; no completeness hypothesis is used.

The support theorem lem-pur-strict-tensor-augmentation-normalization assembles the coordinate and extensionality results of lem-pur-strict-tensor-augmentation-coordinates: product projections agree by pure-tensor extensionality, both second coordinates vanish, mapping-cocone extensionality identifies the components, and natural-transformation extensionality proves uniqueness. The assigned theorem applies this fully proved existence-and-uniqueness statement after unfolding its original normalization predicate.

For tensorAugmentation_isIso, apply finiteTorOrdinaryTensorComplete to the two derived inputs, with precisely their stated finite-Tor constructibility hypotheses. The calculus integralTensorModel.iso identifies the localization of the ordinary signed total tensor with this complete ordinary derived tensor. The canonicalCompletionUnitCriterion and naturality across this isomorphism imply invertibility of the specified completion unit on the localized ordinary total.

The ordinary total of the two good complexes is itself good by IntegralAmbient.tensor_good. Evaluate completionUnit_existsUnique on that total. Its normalization expresses Q of the strict roosUnit as the already invertible derived completion unit followed by completionComparison.hom, hence Q(roosUnit) is invertible.

The existing map_normalized helper proves that StrictTensorAugmentation.map satisfies the strict normalization predicate, retaining both coordinate equations. Unfold the selected witness specification and use uniqueness to identify tensorAugmentation with that constructed map. Its component formula is roosUnit followed by the Roos image of tensorTowerIso.hom. Functoriality of Q and preservation and composition of isomorphisms prove tensorAugmentation_isIso without additional hypotheses on the scheme.

For tensorToOrdinary_existsUnique, preserve finite-Tor constructibility under isomorphisms. The integral constructible predicate is closed under isomorphisms by lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated. Retain the existing uniform Tor interval and compose every scalar-reduction presentation with the inverse of the induced isomorphism.

Pairs of good complexes localize to pairs of derived objects, and precomposition along this localization is fully faithful, by lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined and Mathlib product localization. Restrict ordinaryModel.representative to these good pairs. Conjugate the localization of the fixed tensorAugmentation by the ordinary and completed representative comparisons and descend the resulting natural transformation uniquely. This step does not assume that the augmentation is invertible on arbitrary derived objects.

On a finite-Tor good pair, tensorAugmentation_isIso, proved by the preceding completion-unit argument, identifies the inverse of tensorToOrdinaryOnGood with the descended transformation component. Naturality and cancellation through the images of representative isomorphisms show that every transported comparison has the same inverse component at the target pair.

Choose a good representative of each input by essential surjectivity of the good localization. Transport their finite-Tor membership by the finite-Tor transport step and form the displayed comparison. The inverse-component equality proves its normalization for every representative pair. Apply that normalization to the chosen pair to prove uniqueness. tensorAugmentation_isIso is proved by the completion-unit argument above; tensorAugmentation_existsUnique is proved by the first two steps.

proof_origin.place: Existing source-transport constructions and localization proofs retained. G1 closes tensorAugmentation_isIso using finiteTorOrdinaryTensorComplete (Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 6.5.5), the canonical completion-unit criterion (Stacks lemma-naive-completion), its good-representative normalization, and the constructed strict tensor augmentation. No new statement or additional geometric hypothesis. ordinaryTotal reuses the existing definitionally equal coefficientTotalTensor presentation to avoid repeated dictionary conversions; the signed tensor and its normalization are unchanged.
